Dear Ms Bell,

Thank you for your message of 6 March.

1) Inspection: the contractor was unable to attend the 6 March slot because of a vehicle breakdown, and the property was not inspected. I am sorry for the wasted wait. He has offered 7 March after 13:00, but I have asked him to confirm that in writing and I will not give you a date until he has. Please let me know whether 7 March after 13:00 works for you, and if not, which afternoons do — you previously said weekday afternoons after 13:00 were generally possible.

2) The damp patch: please keep the area ventilated where you can, avoid putting furniture or fabrics against that wall, and do not attempt to strip or dry the paint yourself. Please do not use the socket under the window if you see any sign of moisture reaching it, and contact us straight away — on 999 if there is any sparking or burning smell — if you notice damp reaching the socket, heat, discolouration around it, a burning smell, or a tripped breaker. If water starts dripping or running, call us immediately.

3) The email you received in error: please do not forward or share it, and please do not delete it for now — our privacy team has asked for it to be preserved while they review the incident. They will contact you directly with confirmation of what to do with it. No action is needed from you in the meantime.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

input.summary:
Open privacy incident running alongside the damp job; a human decision is outstanding and the affected parties are waiting.

Facts: (1) The appointment confirmation sent to Iris Bell on 2025-03-05 contained another tenant's name, address, arrears amount and payment arrangement (event-013). (2) Iris reported it the same day, said she had not forwarded it, and asked what to do with it (event-014); she was asked by phone not to forward or share it and said it is still in her inbox (event-015). (3) The incident was logged with Elena Frost, Privacy Lead, with the data categories involved (event-016); Elena asked for preservation and details (event-017) and Maya Chen answered: addressed to Iris only, no attachment, other tenant not yet contacted (event-018). (4) No assessment, no notification decision and no contact with the affected tenant is recorded in the visible history. (5) Iris asked again on 2025-03-06 whether she should keep the email (event-020).

Decisions needed by a human (outside the agent's mandate): whether this is a notifiable personal-data breach (72-hour clock from awareness, 2025-03-05 11:29), whether and when to notify the other tenant whose data was disclosed, and the instruction to Iris on retention or deletion of the message.

Agent action taken: Iris has been told to preserve the email, not to forward it, and that the privacy team will contact her directly (no commitment made on notification or deletion). No contact made with the other tenant and no assessment made — those are reserved for the privacy lead. The maintenance side continues separately: contractor asked to confirm a new inspection window, tenant asked to confirm access, owner updated.
